R1_leader_persists_with_churn.desc: Q0 leader still leads at Q16 (or end) in 40-85% of seeds, and a durable (>=2q) lead change happens in 35-90%
R1_leader_persists_with_churn.why: The real race has had a sticky leader with real challengers; never or always changing is a toy.

R2_revenue_catches_up.desc: Capex/revenue falls from Q0-7 to Q12-20 in 50-95% of seeds; median Q0-7 ratio 1.3-6
R2_revenue_catches_up.why: Build-out runs ahead of revenue early, then revenue grows into it; a ratio that never falls is a bubble with no story, one that always falls is too tidy.

R3_warning_shots_precede_regulation.desc: 60-95% of regulate_on follow a same-bloc public incident within 4q, and that share beats the base rate of such windows by >=0.15
R3_warning_shots_precede_regulation.why: Governments mostly regulate after visible harm, not on a schedule; 100% would mean no anticipatory rules at all, which also isn't true.

R4_pacts_rare_and_short.desc: Pacts form in 15-60% of seeds; median pact lifetime 2-6 quarters
R4_pacts_rare_and_short.why: Voluntary lab restraint commitments are uncommon and erode within a year or two; permanent pacts or none at all are both unrealistic.

R5_laggards_open_weights.desc: Open-weight releases in 30-95% of seeds; 70-95% of releases from true rank>=3 at release
R5_laggards_open_weights.why: Open weights are mostly a challenger's move, but near-frontier labs have released too; 100% laggard share is too clean.

R6_accelerate_before_restraint.desc: First government action is subsidy/export control in 60-95% of seeds with any action
R6_accelerate_before_restraint.why: Major states subsidized and restricted exports before they regulated, but some (EU-style) regulated first, so 100% is too clean.

R7_backlash_sometimes.desc: Physical disruption from public backlash in 10-60% of seeds
R7_backlash_sometimes.why: Physical backlash against AI is possible but not routine.

R8_boom_then_bust.desc: Sentiment rises >=30% then falls >=30% from its peak in 15-70% of seeds
R8_boom_then_bust.why: Investment manias usually overshoot and correct, but a correction is not guaranteed within ten years.

R9_bloc_competition.desc: Bloc B wins 10-45% of takeoffs that have a winner
R9_bloc_competition.why: The second bloc is a real contender but behind on chips and capital; near-zero or parity wins both look wrong.

I1_outcome_variety.why: Replays should feel different, but not like a die roll with no structure.

I2_no_inevitable_winner.desc: Top winning role takes 30-65% of takeoff wins
I2_no_inevitable_winner.why: The favourite should be favoured, not inevitable; under 30% means roles stopped mattering.

I3_unknowns_matter.desc: Max |r| of a hidden unknown with catastrophe or takeoff time is 0.25-0.85
I3_unknowns_matter.why: Hidden world parameters should shape the story, but not decide it alone; above 0.85 choices barely matter.

I4_actors_react.desc: Lab switch rate in the 2q after a public incident or sentiment crash is 1.2-5x the background rate
I4_actors_react.why: Actors should visibly respond to shocks; over 5x means they only ever move on shocks.

I5_beliefs_diverge.desc: Median end-of-run hazard-belief spread across actors is 0.15-0.60 of the prior range
I5_beliefs_diverge.why: Different roles should read the same evidence differently, but not live in unrelated worlds.
